title: Finite type coherent relations on an iterated open slice
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, $U\subseteq X$ open, and $\mathcal G$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] in the module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $V=(W\hookrightarrow U)$ be an object of the open slice, so $W\subseteq U$ is open. For every finite set $I$ and morphism $f:((\mathcal O_X|_U)|_V)^{\oplus I}\to (\mathcal G|_U)|_V$ on the iterated slice, $\ker f$ is of finite type.

source.place: Modules, Definition 01BV (definition-coherent), condition (2), applied to W; open-restriction convention in Lemma 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), proof of (2). Verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01BV and /tag/01BY.

proof.text: Write V as W contained in U. Forgetting the intermediate inclusion into U identifies an object Z -> V of the iterated slice with Z -> W in the slice over W; the inverse inserts Z -> U. Because inclusions in the poset of opens are unique, these functors are inverse up to the canonical isomorphisms. Both sites have the same rings, restriction maps and covering sieves. The identification transports sheaves of modules, finite free modules and their maps.

Choose a bijection I with ULift(Fin n), where n is the finite cardinality of I. Transport f to the resulting map from the rank-n free module to G restricted to W. The second clause of coherence at W makes its kernel finite type. Identify the kernels by their sectionwise universal properties. Pull back the finite local generator families along the site identification; the cover and epi conditions are unchanged because all section maps and covering sieves agree. Thus kernel f is finite type, including I empty or W empty.
